#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  You play $DUSK  nodes: roll the interest you’ve earned directly into an older position—almost everyone defaults to this kind of move. @Dusk_Foundation ’s proposed plan sounds great at first glance: instead of starting a new node and waiting 6 to 12 hours, just add to the old pool. Suppose you top up with 10,000 tokens: 9,000 tokens can instantly enter the active state to mine, while the remaining 1,000 tokens become locked. You sacrifice 10% liquidity to get 90% of your funds working immediately—on the face of it, you’re definitely not losing.

But long-term players quickly discover the hidden reefs. The key issue is the “reinvestment frequency.” Every time you roll profits back in, the system will consistently skim off one-tenth and lock it as a stagnant state. That money is still under your name, but it produces zero returns. Stretch the timeline out: if you add a total of 100,000 tokens in batches, roughly 10,000 tokens will gradually turn into “dead chips.” When you calculate your real return rate, that capital tied up and locked away will drag down your overall profits severely.

Even more tormenting is that retrieving these idle, stuck assets is quite cumbersome. According to the official instructions, when certain conditions occur, you must take the entire node’s chips out as a whole—everything—then fully unbind. Unbinding is fast, but if you want to start staking for yield again, the entire position has to go through that same 6 to 12 hour queue just to reactivate. In other words, the time you carefully squeezed out day-to-day through reinvestment ends up being given back when you finally reorganize the holdings—and during that period, the account’s earnings basically drop to zero.

Once you understand this mechanism, you realize the rule is a double-edged sword. Forcing locked shares does indeed reduce some immediate sell pressure, but it contributes nothing to on-chain consensus security. And if major node operators collectively pull back to activate idle funds, a large amount of chips will temporarily return to the liquid market. So don’t let long-term investors be fooled by an inflated “total staking rate.” Focus on the true proportion of active chips, the size of idle locked funds, and how often big players queue to reorganize—only then can you see whether this compounding game is truly generating returns for you, or effectively trapping your principal.#eth $ETH

然而，长线玩家很快就会摸到其中的暗礁。症结就在“加仓频率”上。你每一次把利润复投，系统都会雷打不动地截留十分之一作为停滞状态。这笔钱虽在你名下，却无法产生任何收益。拉长周期看，假如你分批追加了累计10万枚，不知不觉就有约1万枚沦为了“死筹码”。核算真实回报率时，这笔被占压的本金会把你的总体利润狠狠拉低。

更折磨人的是，想把这笔趴窝的资产捞出来，流程相当繁杂。按官方提示，遇到特定情况你必须把整个节点的筹码连锅端，全部解绑。解绑固然快，可一旦想再次质押生息，全仓资金又得重新去熬那6到12小时的排队激活。等于说，你靠日常复投精打细算抠出来的时间，在最终重组仓位时全吐了回去，期间整个账户的收益彻底挂零。

搞懂这套玩法就知道，该规则对盘面是把双刃剑。强制 locked 的份额确实锁死了部分抛压，但对链上共识安全毫无贡献。并且，一旦大节点为了盘活闲钱集体退仓，大量筹码会短暂重返流通市场。所以，长线投资别被虚高的“总质押率”忽悠了。盯紧 active 筹码的真实占比、闲置 locked 的体量，以及大户重组排队的频率，才能看透这场复利游戏到底是在替你创收，还是在变相圈禁你的本金。#eth $ETH

【If ETH drops another 200 yuan, how many people would die in the market】

Honestly, recently I’ve been getting private messages from people in the background asking me whether they can still hold ETH. I don’t know how to answer, either. Why? Because I’m not sure myself.

Right now the chart is basically one word: chop. At $ 1880, it’s neither up nor down. In the past 24 hours it’s only down 0.6%, and over a week it’s down just 1%. It doesn’t look painful, right? But the problem is exactly here—trading volume is incredibly low. Everyone is waiting. Waiting for what? Waiting for someone else to move first.

FNG is 29, and the weekly average is also 29. What does this indicate? It means panic hasn’t worsened further, but don’t expect anyone to be bold enough to buy the dip. Market sentiment right now is like a tamed animal—everyone is scared to move, because they’ve already been traumatized by the huge bull-and-bear swings of 2021.

BTC dominance is still at 56.2%, standing there like it owns the place. The “big brother” behavior of pooling funds hasn’t changed. ETH may have opportunities, but the funds simply aren’t going. In this kind of setup, can ETH independently move up strongly? Hard to say.

Some people will say Goldman Sachs acquiring NEOS is a positive. Sure, let’s call it a positive. But I want to ask: for this $2.25B acquisition, what exactly will it do for ETH holders? Will the ETF size increase? Okay. Then what—trading fees go down? Or annualized returns go up? Honestly, large institutions’ positioning is based on long-term logic. They can’t control the short-term market.

Bitmine’s 257M annualized staking income is similar. It sounds impressive, but that’s the institution’s business. What does it have to do with you, a small retail investor who actually holds a position?

Right now, when I look at ETH, I’m basically watching. $ 1850 is support. If it breaks, then $ 1750 is next. Resistance? $ 1950. Getting there in the short term won’t be easy. The direction is close to being decided, but unless volume increases, I’d rather not move.

What’s your mindset right now? If you have a position, are you going to hold on for dear life, or did you trim? If you’re in cash with no position—would you dare to enter around here? Anyway, what I say doesn’t matter. After I finish talking, if you’re itchy, you’ll still be itchy.

The S&P 500 closes at a new all-time high again

The performance of U.S. benchmark indexes has once again become a focal point for global risk assets. According to compiled financial information, the S&P 500 closed at a new all-time high in the latest trading session. The result was quickly discussed by the market and incorporated into a framework for monitoring macro sentiment.

In terms of background, the S&P 500—widely seen as the key gauge of the overall performance of large U.S. listed companies—has long been regarded as an important barometer of global risk appetite. Its constituents span multiple heavily weighted sectors, including technology, consumer, financials, and industrials. Whether the index can continue to set fresh records at elevated levels often reflects the market’s combined pricing of expectations for economic growth, the resilience of corporate earnings, and the prevailing liquidity environment. When the index breaks to new highs at the close rather than only intraday, it typically suggests that buy-side strength has been relatively dominant throughout the trading day, making the closing price a more representative measure.

On the core facts, what can currently be confirmed is this: the S&P 500 closed at a new all-time high. Public materials highlighted it as one of the day’s key financial items. It should be noted that the existing evidence mainly confirms the outcome itself—“closing at a new high”—without fully disclosing the specific closing level, the contribution by each sector, changes in trading value, or the precise percentage difference versus the prior peak. Therefore, it would be inappropriate to overextend conclusions into the fine-driving details. Other macro variables mentioned alongside the index include long-end U.S. Treasury yields, exchange rates, and commodity prices; however, the evidence does not provide a verifiable, quantified breakdown of their causal weight relative to the S&P 500’s new high. They can only be treated as parallel items to observe.

As for the logic behind index closing at a new high, it usually carries several implications. First, a rebalancing of earnings and valuation: if leading companies’ earnings reports and forward guidance are steady, the index is more likely to rise under the influence of heavy-weight stocks. Second, a repricing of liquidity and rate expectations: when the market believes the policy path can still be matched to the pricing of risk assets, the resistance to further index highs may relatively decline. Third, confirmation from fund-flow behavior: a closing-price break tends to reflect the combined effect of institutional positioning and passive capital more than an intraday surge. At the same time, it’s important to recognize the other side: a new index high does not automatically mean the market’s internal structure is healthy. If the rally is concentrated in a handful of heavy weights and breadth is lacking, or if volatility and trading activity do not expand in tandem, the new high more likely reflects “strength at the index level” rather than a broad-based advance. In the absence of simultaneous breadth data and detailed fund-flow information, the above structural assessment can only serve as a framework-level prompt, not a confirmed conclusion.

The transmission path to the crypto market is more about the propagation of risk appetite rather than a one-to-one, immediate mapping. Traditionally, when U.S. stocks—especially benchmark indexes like the S&P 500—strengthen, market risk appetite often improves. Some capital may become more tolerant of high-volatility assets, allowing crypto assets to benefit indirectly from a rebound in risk sentiment. When technology growth styles lead, the market is also more likely to link liquidity-loosening expectations with growth narratives, creating a sentiment-level resonance in crypto pricing. Conversely, if a new stock index high coincides with a significant rise in Treasury yields, a stronger U.S. dollar, or repeated swings in liquidity expectations, risk assets internally could see a “stocks strong, coins diverge” scenario. Based on the evidence available today, what can be confirmed is the macro backdrop of the benchmark U.S. index closing at a new high. Whether the crypto market also increases in volume, and which sectors are more sensitive, still depends on subsequent liquidity, regulation, and event-driven factors—it cannot be directly extrapolated from a single index outcome.

The editorial takeaway and observation is: it is more appropriate to understand “the S&P 500 closing at a new historical high” as a set of macro sentiment signals, rather than as a single trading instruction. For observers of crypto and other risk assets, more value lies in tracking the quality of confirmation after the new high— including the depth of pullbacks, whether trading activity keeps pace, whether interest rates and the U.S. dollar form hedging pressure, and whether the linkages between risk assets remain stable. At the factual level, currently only the index closing at a refreshed historical peak can be confirmed. Whether the rally is sustainable and whether it will create a continued spillover into the crypto market remains speculative and requires later data verification. Overall, this event strengthens the narrative that “global risk assets continue to price growth and liquidity at elevated levels,” but it also serves as a reminder: a new high is not the endpoint—structure and constraint conditions are equally critical.

content:
美股标普500指数收盘再创历史新高

美股基准指数走势再度成为全球风险资产关注焦点。据相关财经汇总信息，标普500指数在最新交易中收盘创下历史新高，这一结果迅速被市场讨论并纳入宏观情绪观察框架。

从事件背景看，标普500指数作为衡量美国大型上市公司整体表现的核心指标，长期被视作全球风险偏好的重要风向标。其成分覆盖科技、消费、金融、工业等多个权重板块，指数能否在高位继续刷新纪录，往往对应着资金对经济增长预期、企业盈利韧性以及流动性环境的综合定价。当指数以收盘价而非仅盘中价刷新高点时，通常意味着多头力量在全天交易中占据相对主导，收盘定价更具代表性。

核心事实方面，目前可确认的信息是：标普500指数收盘创历史新高。公开材料将其作为当日财经要点之一予以强调。需要说明的是，现有证据主要确认“收盘创新高”这一结果本身，并未完整披露具体收盘点位、分板块贡献、成交额变化，以及与前高之间的精确幅度；因此，对驱动细节不宜过度延伸。与指数同步被提及的，还有美债长端收益率、汇率与商品价格等宏观变量，但它们与本次标普创新高之间的因果权重，证据并未给出可核验的量化拆解，只能作为并列观察项。

逻辑拆解上，指数收盘创新高通常包含几层含义。其一，是盈利与估值的再平衡：若龙头公司财报与前瞻指引偏稳，指数更容易在权重股带动下抬升；其二，是流动性与利率预期的再定价：当市场认为政策路径尚可匹配风险资产定价时，股指冲高的阻力会相对下降；其三，是资金行为层面的确认，收盘价刷新往往比盘中冲高更能反映机构仓位与被动资金的共同作用。但也要看到另一面：指数新高并不自动等于市场内部结构健康，若上涨集中在少数权重、广度不足，或波动率与成交并未同步放大，则新高更多体现“指数层面的强”，而非“全面普涨”。在缺少同步广度与资金流向明细的情况下，上述结构判断只能作为框架性提示，而非已证实结论。

对加密市场的影响路径，更多体现为风险偏好的传导，而非一一对应的即时映射。传统上，当美股尤其是标普等基准指数走强时，市场风险胃口往往改善，部分资金对高波动资产的容忍度上升，加密资产可能间接受益于风险情绪回暖；科技成长风格占优时，市场也更容易把流动性宽松预期与成长叙事联系起来，从而对加密定价形成情绪层面的共振。反过来，若股指新高伴随美债收益率显著抬升、美元走强或流动性预期反复，则风险资产内部可能出现“股强而币分化”的局面。就当前证据而言，能够确认的是美股基准指数收盘创新高这一宏观背景，加密市场是否同步放量、哪些板块更敏感，仍取决于后续流动性、监管与事件驱动，不能由单一股指结果直接外推。

编辑判断与观察是：把“标普500收盘历史新高”理解为一组宏观情绪信号，比理解成单一交易指令更合适。对加密与风险资产观察者而言，更有价值的是跟踪新高之后的确认质量——包括回撤幅度、成交是否跟上、利率与美元是否形成对冲压力，以及风险资产之间的联动是否稳定。事实层面，目前仅能确认指数收盘刷新历史高点；关于上涨是否可持续、会否向加密市场形成持续溢出，仍属推测，需要后续数据验证。整体上，这一事件强化了“全球风险资产仍在高位定价增长与流动性”的叙事，但也提醒市场：新高本身不是终点，结构与约束条件同样关键。

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  On Friday, I翻了翻 the core source code of Dusk ($DUSK) consensus.rs. Objectively speaking, its three-layer verification mechanism paired with the Kadcast protocol—claimed to save half the traffic—really is impressive in terms of architectural ideas. But when I focused on the variable EMERGENCY_MODE_ITERATION_THRESHOLD, my confidence instantly dropped.

This so-called “emergency mode” is supposed to be a safety cushion when the system lags, but the source code doesn’t clearly explain what the actual trigger threshold is. In a crisis, who packages those special blocks, and what exactly are the validation criteria? Official documentation is completely clueless. This kind of black-box setting, once deployed on the mainnet, is extremely easy for hackers to maliciously target.

Go check Issue #1907 and you’ll find that this logic was already criticized by peers long ago. With the current code, as soon as the iteration count runs out, the counter is blindly reset to zero and the process is restarted. That means the worse the network environment is, the more nodes will spin in place going nowhere. Even though the community suggested optimizing it into a “state suspend,” nothing has ever been implemented—talk without practice.

What really makes your scalp tingle is Issue #2361. Imagine: if a large number of nodes simultaneously fall behind and collectively switch into emergency mode, the system will drive them to instantly send GetBlocks requests in perfect synchrony. With no rate limiting and no buffering—this was intended as self-rescue, but it directly turns into a DDoS attack that knocks its own mainnet over, instantly exhausting bandwidth.

And then, on top of Kadcast’s underwhelming performance, it’s even more disastrous. In early tests with very small scale, even broadcasting couldn’t achieve 100% coverage. Dusk is highly dependent on multi-round node confirmations; if a single packet gets lost, consensus is likely to time out. Once it times out, it triggers that emergency mode full of traps again—an vicious cycle born right there.

All things considered, at its current stage, Dusk’s mechanism is far from a secure foundation; instead, it feels more like a mine that could explode at any time. #eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  周五翻了翻 Dusk ($DUSK) 的核心源码 consensus.rs。客观讲，它的三层验证机制搭配号称能省一半流量的 Kadcast 协议，架构构思确实惊艳。但当我盯上 EMERGENCY_MODE_ITERATION_THRESHOLD 这个变量时，心里瞬间没底了。

这个“紧急模式”本该是系统卡顿时的安全垫，但源码里根本没交待清楚触发底线是多少。危机时特殊区块由谁打包、校验标准是什么？官方资料毫无头绪。这种黑盒设定，一旦上主网极易被黑客恶意针对。

去翻翻 Issue #1907 就会发现，这套逻辑早就被同行吐槽了。按现有代码，只要迭代次数耗尽，计数器就无脑清零重跑。这意味着网络环境越差，节点越是原地疯狂空转。虽然社区建议优化成“状态挂起”，但一直没见落地，光说不练。

真正让人头皮发麻的是 Issue #2361。试想，如果大批节点同时掉队并集体切进紧急状态，系统会驱使它们瞬间齐刷刷地发送 GetBlocks 请求。毫无限流和缓冲，这本意是自救，结果直接演变成了搞垮自家主网的 DDoS 攻击，瞬间榨干带宽。

再叠加上 Kadcast 协议的拉胯表现，就更要命了。早期极小规模的测试中，发个广播都无法做到百分百覆盖。Dusk 可是高度依赖多轮节点确认的，底层一丢包，共识就容易超时；一超时，又去触发那个到处是坑的紧急模式，恶性循环就此诞生。

盘点下来，Dusk 现阶段这套机制离安全底座相去甚远，反而更像是个随时会自爆的雷。#eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  A few days ago I took some time to look into Dusk’s backend code (mainly consensus.rs). Honestly, the SA consensus mechanism described in their whitepaper is pretty interesting: proposals, validation, and confirmation are handled by three different node committees. They also claim that Kadcast can save half the traffic for transmission. But when I saw the parameter EMERGENCY_MODE_ITERATION_THRESHOLD, I felt uneasy. This so-called “emergency fallback” doesn’t seem as reliable as the宣传 makes it out to be. Even the triggering conditions, emergency block production, and validation logic are all unclear—there’s not even a trace of it in the public documentation.

Digging through their GitHub history is even more striking—this part had already been raised as an Issue. For example, #1907 pointed out that after nodes time out in the last round of block production, the counter simply gets reset and they rerun. That means once the network gets bad, nodes will just get stuck in this dead loop, hard-working at it over and over. The community previously discussed changing it to “pause and keep state while stuck,” but so far the code still hasn’t changed, and handling of edge cases is quite rough.

By the time you get to Issue #2361, it gets even worse. Suppose there’s widespread disconnect on-chain and all network nodes are forced into emergency mode together. The result is that everyone simultaneously spams the whole network with GetBlocks requests to pull data. Because the necessary request rate-limiting mechanism is missing, what was originally meant to prevent deadlock turns into a traffic bombing against their own mainnet—instantly exhausting all bandwidth.

And looking at the underlying Kadcast: when they previously tested at small scale with 10 nodes, the messages still couldn’t be broadcast to everyone. Public chains like Dusk rely on frequent packet exchanges among committees to run consensus. If broadcasts miss packets, consensus times out; once it times out, it repeatedly collides with that immature emergency mode, and all kinds of risks end up stringing together like a fuse.

In my view, once Dusk’s unfinished emergency mode ($DUSK) is deployed on the real mainnet, it’s likely not a cure, but a hidden risk introduced into the system. I hope the team can fill in the underlying broadcasting and add proper request rate-limiting as soon as possible. #eth $ETH

content:
#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  前几天抽空研究了下 Dusk 的后端代码（主要是 consensus.rs 那块）。讲真，他们白皮书里写的那套 SA 共识机制挺有意思，搞了提案、校验和确认三个不同的节点委员会，再加上 Kadcast 说是能给传输省下一半流量。但等我看到 EMERGENCY_MODE_ITERATION_THRESHOLD 这行参数时，心里就有点打鼓了。这所谓的“紧急兜底”根本不像宣传的那么靠谱，连触发条件、应急出块和验证逻辑都是糊涂账，公开文档里连字影都没有。

去翻他们的 GitHub 记录更刺眼，这部分其实早被发了 Issue。比如 #1907 就指出来：现在节点在最后一轮出块超时后，计数器会直接清零重跑。这意味着一旦遇到糟糕的网络，节点只会卡在这个死循环里硬折腾。社区之前讨论说要改成“卡住挂起保持状态”，但至今代码里依然没动静，边缘状况下的处理相当粗糙。

到了 Issue #2361，问题就更严重了。假设链上出现了大面积掉线，全网节点被迫一起进紧急模式，结果就是大家同时向全网狂发 GetBlocks 请求拉数据。因为缺了必要的请求限速机制，这套原本用来防卡死的回退机制，反而会秒变针对自己主网的流量轰炸，瞬间把所有带宽吃干抹净。

再看看底层的 Kadcast，其实之前小规模跑 10 个节点测试时，消息都没法做到全员播发。Dusk 这类公链是全靠委员会频繁发包交互来跑共识的，广播只要漏包，共识就得超时；一超时就频繁撞上那套不成熟的紧急模式，各种隐患直接串成了一根引线。

在我看来，Dusk（$DUSK）这个未完工的紧急模式一旦上了真实主网，很可能不是解药，而是给系统埋下了隐患。希望团队能尽快把底层的广播和请求限速补齐吧。#eth $ETH

title: 🔄 八年研究、数千万美元打水漂？以太坊基金会正式放弃L1的Poseidon哈希
subTitle:
#以太坊基金会L1弃用Poseidon哈希 
8月13日，以太坊基金会研究员Justin Drake在X平台发文宣布：以太坊基金会决定在L1层放弃Poseidon哈希函数，转向SHA或BLAKE等传统哈希函数。
这一决定结束了自2018年以来长达八年、耗资数千万美元的后量子密码学探索。
🔍 Poseidon是什么？为什么放弃？
Poseidon是2019年诞生的“SNARK友好型”哈希函数，专为零知识证明系统优化设计，被大量zkRollup和zkVM使用，保障着数十亿美元级别的资产安全。
放弃的核心原因不是Poseidon本身出了问题，而是SNARK设计取得了突破性进展：
· 通过 “二进制域”（binary field） 运算方式，传统哈希函数（SHA/BLAKE）在SNARK电路中的性能已可媲美Poseidon
· 单台笔记本电脑每秒可完成约100万次传统哈希调用验证，仅有约100倍的CPU开销
· 范式从“为SNARK优化哈希”转向了 “为哈希优化SNARK” 
⚠️ 另一个关键因素：安全性
随着AI密码分析能力的提升，部分后量子密码方案近期相继遭受攻击——格密码方案HAWK和同源密码方案SQIsign均出现安全挫折。
相比之下，SHA和BLAKE这类经过数十年审查的传统哈希函数，已知攻击向量更少，部署速度可能更快。以太坊基金会甚至专门启动了100万美元的Poseidon密码分析计划来压力测试，最终仍倾向于更成熟的替代方案。
📅 后续时间线：
· 2027年：推出生产级leanVM
· 2028年：部署到以太坊的共识层、数据层和执行层
Justin Drake表示，这些日期仍属初步计划。
🔗 对相关代币的可能影响：
· $ETH：决策本身对以太坊长期安全架构是利好——转向经过数十年验证的传统哈希，后量子抗性更明确。但短期内属技术面调整，对ETH价格直接影响有限。
· ZK赛道代币（$ZK、$STRK等）：Poseidon被L1放弃，但Drake明确表示Poseidon目前仍通过zkRollup和zkVM保障着数十亿级别资产。对已部署的ZK项目暂无直接影响，但新项目可能会重新评估哈希方案选择。
· AI/Crypto交叉概念：AI密码分析能力的提升加速了此次决策，这一逻辑可能被市场短期炒作。
💡 怎么看？
这是一次罕见的 “技术路线大转向” ——以太坊基金会花了八年时间、数千万美元押注Poseidon，最终因为SNARK技术本身进步太快而主动放弃。传统哈希在ZK电路里跑出了接近Poseidon的性能，再加上数十年安全审计积累的信任优势，Poseidon的“专属优势”消失了。
有时候，最好的创新不是发明新东西，而是让旧东西变得足够好。
投资有风险，决策需谨慎。本文仅作信息分享，不构成任何投资建议。
---

translatedData.subTitle:
<t-99/>#以太坊基金会L1弃用Poseidon哈希 
On August 13, Justin Drake, a researcher at the Ethereum Foundation, posted on the X platform announcing that the Ethereum Foundation has decided to abandon the Poseidon hash function on the L1 layer and move to traditional hash functions such as SHA or BLAKE.
This decision ends the eight-year, multi-hundred-million-dollar exploration of post-quantum cryptography that began in 2018.
🔍 What is Poseidon? Why was it abandoned?
Poseidon is a “SNARK-friendly” hash function created in 2019, optimized specifically for zero-knowledge proof systems. It is widely used by zkRollups and zkVMs, helping to ensure the security of assets worth billions of dollars.

Position sizing needs to differentiate between spot and contracts. title: Crypto Market Update: Bitcoin Range Persists as SEC Delay, ETF Flows and Tokenization Drive Sentiment
subTitle:
Bitcoin remains range-bound as traders weigh U.S. policy, ETF flows and security headlines. CoinDesk reported that BTC has spent weeks around a $62,000 to $66,000 range, with ETF buying offset by miner and corporate-holder selling while volatility stays low. The latest tone is cautious rather than deeply bearish: the market has support, but it still lacks the volume needed for a convincing breakout.

Regulation is the dominant macro story. Investor's Business Daily reported that the SEC and OCC are still moving crypto policy forward even as the Senate delays the CLARITY Act until after recess. The SEC's broader Regulation Crypto agenda and the OCC's openness to crypto-related bank charters point to a more formal market structure, but not instant clarity. That uncertainty can keep capital selective.

ETF flows are another pressure point. CoinStats noted that U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF flows flipped negative by about $61.1 million on August 12, while ETH ETFs stayed modestly positive. This does not erase the institutional story, but it does mean bulls need renewed inflows to keep defending the range.

The Block's latest feed also highlights two themes to watch: Bitwise exploring tokenization of its Solana staking ETF through Superstate, and Tether receiving a clean KPMG opinion in its first full audit. Tokenization and stablecoin transparency both remain key institutional narratives.

For traders, the playbook remains patient. BTC, ETH and liquid altcoins may react sharply to policy and ETF headlines, but sustained trend needs stronger volume, renewed flows and cleaner regulatory signals. #BTC #ETH #Crypto #ETF #Macro

【If ETH breaks below 1700, what the big players do is more interesting than the price itself】

Let’s talk about a few on-chain signals from this week.

First, the news about Goldman Sachs acquiring NEOS—its $ 30 billion deal involves an ETF business, and ETH-related products are included as well. Institutions are putting real money on the table, which is more substantive than just slogans. But the question is—if institutions come in, can ETH automatically go up? Back in 2017, institutions were still watching from the sidelines. That didn’t stop prices from rising—or falling. So when I read this news, my takeaway is simple: someone is planning, but planning and “harvesting” are two different things.

What’s truly interesting are several signals revealed by on-chain data.

The ETH holdings in the wallets of big players have been quietly increasing, while retail holders are running out. I’ve seen this playbook before—early 2021 was exactly like this. Once the concentration of big players’ chips rises, the next move is usually either a burst of momentum or a sign that the main forces are preparing to distribute. At this point, we can’t tell which yet, but one thing is certain: it isn’t retail buying.

Exchange net flows have recently leaned toward inflows, suggesting that someone is preparing to sell. Coupled with subdued trading volume, it also hints that market sentiment is cautious—before deciding on a direction, everyone is waiting.

Active addresses are declining, but the number of addresses holding for more than a year is rising. Put together, this is pretty intriguing: short-term participants are withdrawing, while long-term holders are waiting. This looks like market rotation, not outright selling.

On valuation: $ 1872 is only one step away from key support at $ 1825. Right now, the market sentiment “FNG” is 29, which sits at the edge of the extreme panic zone. Valuation being low is true, but undervaluation doesn’t automatically mean an immediate rally. In the second half of 2018, valuations were also low, yet prices still drifted lower for half a year.

Honestly, what I care about now is whether Goldman’s acquisition can translate into real business expansion for ETH. If the ETF scale really gets going, that would be the big-picture logic that benefits ETH as well. But if it’s only financial-layer M&A integration, the short-term impact is likely limited.

In practice, it comes down to whether institutional ETF products can truly attract money to flow in. It’s still early, so I won’t make a conclusion yet.

What’s everyone’s mindset right now? Do you want to add here, or are you looking to run? Are you getting itchy?

【如果ETH跌破1700，大户们的反应比价格本身更有意思】

说说链上这周的几个信号。

先说高盛收购NEOS这件事$ 30亿的ETF业务，ETH相关产品也在里面。机构在用真金白银表态，这比喊口号实在。但问题是——机构进来了，ETH就能涨吗？2017年那会儿机构还在观望呢，不耽误涨也不耽误跌。所以这条消息我看完就一个感受：有人在布局，但布局和收割是两回事。

真正有意思的是链上数据透出来的几个信号。

大户钱包的ETH持仓在悄悄增加，散户在往外跑。这套路我见过——2021年年初就是这样，大户筹码集中度一上来，后面要么走出一波行情，要么就是主力在出货前兆，现在还判断不了。但有一点可以确定：不是散户在买。

交易所净流量最近偏向流入，说明有人在准备卖。配合成交量低迷来看，市场观望情绪重，选择方向前大家都在等。

活跃地址数在下降，但持币超过1年的地址数量在上升。这两件事放一起挺有意思——短期的人在撤，长期的人在等。这是市场在换手，不是抛售。

估值这块，$ 1872离关键支撑$ 1825就差一步。现在市场情绪FNG才29，属于极度恐慌区间的边缘。估值低是真的，但低估不代表马上涨，2018年下半年估值也低，照样阴跌了大半年。

说真的，我现在关心的是高盛这笔收购后续能不能给ETH带来实际的业务增量。如果ETF规模真的做起来，那是大饼ETH都受益的大逻辑。如果只是金融层面的并购整合，短期影响有限。

这种事落到实处，就是看机构的ETF产品能不能真的吸引到钱进来。现在还早，我不下结论。

The just-submitted order for 62,800 got smashed through.

I stared at the screen for two seconds.

My first reaction was to add more to average down.

Wait.

That money is already lost—whether I buy something now has nothing to do with it.

But the human brain doesn’t recognize that logic.

It only remembers how much I put in here, and it can’t bear to let those numbers be wasted.

Today, BTC’s current price is $62,774, down 1.58% over the past 24 hours, with trading volume of only 734 million U.

Low-volume, slow drift lower—there isn’t much sentiment in the market.

But precisely in times like this, it’s easiest to trick yourself with “since I’m already down so much anyway.”

Before adding to your position, ask yourself:

If I were currently in cash with no position, would I still buy at this level?

If the answer is hesitation, don’t let your old position hold your new decision hostage.

What you lose is a sunk cost—not a reason to buy.

Don’t let losses place orders for you.

#BTC #ETH #投资哲学 #交易心态 #crypto circle

Ethereum made a decision that looks like surrender, but is actually very mature.

They spent eight years and poured eight-figure dollars into developing a hashing algorithm specifically designed for zero-knowledge proofs. Yesterday, the Foundation announced: give it up, and switch to SHA and BLAKE—old standards that have been used worldwide for decades.

The reason isn’t that the work failed; it’s that the proof technology itself has advanced, and the older algorithms are now fast enough too. The researchers’ exact words were very precise: the key isn’t “a proof-friendly hash,” but “a hash-friendly proof.”

📌 This is exactly two sides of the same coin as the Coldcard incident I wrote about on August 1—back then, it was a problem with their custom random number generator, and 594 bitcoins were stolen.

You tell me: if eight years of results can be discarded like that, do you think it’s a waste, or a reasonable judgment? Comment and let’s discuss.$ETH $BTC

title: 🔸 总览定调
subTitle:
🔸 总览定调

📈 看涨

这波 trending 榜单其实挺有意思,嗯,前几名清一色小市值暴力拉升,Fusionist 24h 134.5%、Akedo 93.7%,夹在中间的几个老面孔反而走得温吞,Uniswap 跌 8.2%、LAB 跌 23%。说白了,资金现在不是雨露均沾,是抱团往几个有故事、有热度的盘子里冲。我看 CoinGecko trending 24h 搜索量这个维度,前几名基本都被 meme 叙事 + 链上新交互占据,真正靠基本面硬撑的反而排到第 4、第 5 位。这会儿咱们就挑三个最有嚼头的聊一聊:Fusionist、Akedo,顺带把 ETHFI 这个 restaking 赛道的小龙头拎出来看看,毕竟它的 12.9% 涨幅说明资金对这条线还没彻底放手。

🔸 Fusionist (ACE) — 单日翻倍的爆发力从哪里来

⚖️ 震荡观望

先说数字:ACE 当前 0.2762 美元,市值排名 #624,24h 涨幅 134.5%(CoinGecko 行情快照,截至撰文)。这种单日翻倍的走势,放在主流币身上几乎不可能出现,只有小盘 + 高换手才能堆出来。按我看,核心催化大致三个:

第一,链上动作。Fusionist 之前一直在做“游戏即挖矿 + 链上 NFT 装备”这套叙事,最近官方释出主线版本更新的预览,把“工业化模拟经营”的概念往前推了一步,关注度一下就上来了。链上持币地址数过去 7 天大概涨了 18%-22%(社区看板数据,具体数字以官方为准),说明新增资金不是机器人,是真人在进场。

第二,交易所端配合。ACE 这两天在多家 CEX 上交易对扩容,USDT、USDC 同步上线,流动性入口被打开,套利盘和趋势盘一起涌入,成交量放大到日均 1.4 亿美元上下,这是它能稳在 0.27 而不是冲高回落的关键。

第三,技术面。EMA20 之前被压在 0.18 附近横了快两周,这一根阳线直接放量穿过 EMA20、EMA60 双线,RSI 14 周期冲到 78,不算极致超买,但已经进入“强势但不泡沫”的区间。我的判断是,这种结构通常还有第二波上探,0.32-0.35 区间是有可能摸到的,但如果日内回踩 0.23 没能撑住,那就要警惕做成双顶。

我会怎么做:不追高。如果回踩 0.21-0.23 区间缩量企稳,我考虑小仓位试多,止损放在 0.19 下方,目标先看 0.30,再观察是否能拓展到 0.35。仓位不超过总资金的 3%,毕竟市值排名还在 600 开外,一天就能翻倍,反过来一天也能腰斩。

🔸 Akedo (AKE) — meme 叙事的余温还是新一轮启动

📈 看涨

AKE 当前 0.0117 美元,市值排名 #134,24h 涨幅 93.7%。按市值看,它已经不算最早期的小盘 meme 了,但 24h 接近翻倍的力度依然夸张。看了一下链上数据,过去 24h 链上交易笔数环比涨了 60% 多,前 100 持有者占比反而从 38% 降到 31%,筹码在往新地址扩散,这是相对健康的信号,至少不是少数地址对倒拉盘。

说白了,AKE 的故事其实很简单:链上 AI agent + 互动式 meme 的混合体。它不像 dogwifhat 那种纯社区 meme,也不像 Pepe 那种纯文化符号,它主打的是“链上 AI 自动生成内容 + 用户互动”,每一笔交易都能触发一个小剧情,这种交互感很容易在 Twitter、Discord 上二次传播。最近一次热度起来,主要是因为某个 KOL 把它跟“以太坊生态的下一个爆款应用”挂钩,虽然这个说法水分很大,但对小盘来说,一句话就够了。

技术上,0.0117 这个位置刚好卡在 2026 年 1 月以来下行通道的上沿,过去三次触碰都被打回来,这次如果能站稳 3-5 天不跌破,通道上破的概率就大很多。我的判断是,这种结构一旦突破,通常会有 30%-50% 的延伸空间,目标先看 0.015-0.017 区间。

我会怎么做:这种小盘最忌讳的是 all-in。AKE 我只会在 0.0098-0.0105 区间缩量回踩时考虑建仓,首仓 2%,止损 0.0085。如果放量站稳 0.0125 上方,再加 1%。目标分两档:0.015 和 0.017,到了先减一半,剩下的让利润跑。

🔸 Ether.fi (ETHFI) — restaking 赛道的真实价值标尺

📈 看涨

ETHFI 这部分我觉得有必要单独拎出来,因为 trending 榜单里大部分都是 meme 和小盘,ETHFI 是为数不多的“有用项目”。当前 0.4257 美元,24h 涨 12.9%,市值排名 #105。按我看,这个涨幅放到大盘身上不值一提,但放在近期 restaking 赛道里其实很有代表性——其他几个同期 restaking 项目 24h 普遍在 5%-8% 之间,ETHFI 能跑出来,说明资金对“真实 TVL + 真实收益”的项目还有偏好。

ETHFI 的核心逻辑不复杂:它是 Ether.fi 协议的治理 + 收益代币,背后挂钩的是以太坊生态的 liquid restaking 业务。链上数据显示,Ether.fi 协议 TVL 最近回到了 38 亿美元附近,比 7 月初的低点反弹了大约 25%,虽然没有回到年内高点的 60 亿美元,但已经是赛道第一。TVL 涨、代币跟涨,这种联动在最近的 restaking 项目里其实不多见。

技术上,ETHFI 过去两周在 0.36-0.45 区间做了一个比较扎实的箱体,0.42 是箱体中轨,12.9% 这一天刚好是中轨突破的确认日。EMA20 从 0.39 抬升到 0.41,EMA60 还在 0.43 上方,意味着上方还有一道压制。我的判断是,这次如果能放量站上 0.45,下一目标看 0.52-0.55 区间,止损放在 0.38 下方比较合理。

我会怎么做:restaking 赛道我本来就配了一部分,ETHFI 我会在回踩 0.40-0.42 区间考虑加仓 1%-2%,跌破 0.38 就先出来观望。目标 0.52 减半,剩下看能不能到 0.55 再做动作。这种仓位我愿意拿久一点,毕竟它不像 meme 那样一天定生死。

🔸 整体仓位思路

⚖️ 震荡观望

按这一波看,我的配置逻辑是“主流底仓 + 卫星小盘 + 赛道对冲”。BTC 和 ETH 还是占大头,大概 50%-55%,剩下 30% 分给 SOL、ENA、ETHFI 这种有真实业务的项目,最后 15%-20% 留给 ACE、AKE 这种 trending 热门小盘。说白了,小盘是用来博弹性的,不是用来压身价的,每一笔都要带止损,仓位控在 3% 以内。

这会儿的市场情绪其实挺微妙,trending 榜单一边是 meme 和小盘暴力拉升,一边是老牌 DeFi 项目还在阴跌,资金没有形成合力。嗯,这种结构下最容易亏钱的就是“FOMO 上车小盘 + 抄底老牌”,两边挨打。所以我给自己的规矩是,小盘只做突破回踩,老牌只做右侧放量,不预判、不抄底、不梭哈。

title: 闪迪逼空还能走多远？秋秋给出1600上方的交易剧本
subTitle:
闪迪逼空还能走多远？秋秋给出1600上方的交易剧本

@天才少女秋秋 这场直播几乎围绕一个核心问题展开：闪迪快速拉升后，究竟是该追随趋势，还是等待冲高做空？她的答案非常明确——短线仍以多头思路为主，但必须把“方向判断”和“仓位管理”分开。她反复强调，不要因为连续上涨就机械猜顶，更不要用币圈常见的多空比、爆仓地图去解释美股盘前与开盘时段的走势。

强势不是做空理由，1600是关键观察位

直播开始时，闪迪已经走出明显加速。秋秋认为，这一段上涨既有存储板块情绪，也叠加了盘前交易、公司消息与空头回补。大量交易者因为“涨得太多”在1500附近逆势开空，反而成为继续逼空的燃料。

她给出的核心条件是：如果价格能够站稳1600，短线就可以继续观察1700一带，强势情况下甚至把1780作为更激进的上方目标。这里的重点不是看到一次上冲便直接认定目标必达，而是观察突破后能否反复守住关键位置。若1600只是瞬间刺穿、随后快速跌回，原有剧本就要重新评估。

秋秋也提醒，越是快速上涨，越不能在高位一次性压重仓。她多次建议只用约2%至4%的小仓位参与，回调时再观察，而不是把“看多”理解成满仓追价。对于强平位置过近的观众，她的处理意见同样直接：先减掉一部分仓位、提高保证金安全垫，活下来比多吃几个点更重要。

闪迪的风险，在于回调往往不是温柔回踩

秋秋虽然坚持看多，却没有把闪迪描述成低风险标的。她认为，闪迪过去的运行特征偏单边：上涨时持续逼空，下跌时也可能连续出现多根阴线。因此，交易者期待的“理想回踩上车”未必会出现；但一旦回调幅度明显扩大，也可能不是普通整理，而是趋势开始反转。

这意味着操作上存在两难：追高会承担突然跳水的风险，等深回调又可能错过整段行情。她给出的解决办法不是预测每一根K线，而是缩小初始仓位、拉远强平线，并提前设定失效条件。尤其在周五临近周末时，流动性下降、资金费率持续累积，持仓体验会明显变差。方向正确也不代表可以忽略时间成本和波动风险。

ETH看反弹，目标先盯1890附近

除了闪迪，秋秋还在直播中多次讨论以太坊。她当时的判断同样偏多，认为短线可以先观察1890附近；如果能够有效突破1900，再看1903一带的延伸空间。她没有把这一段定义成无条件的大级别反转，而是更偏向于一笔短线反弹交易。

她同时指出，比特币和以太坊在美股走强时可能受到资金分流影响，因此不能只看币圈内部情绪。若以太坊迟迟无法收复关键位置，或者反弹过程中量价配合不足，就不应因为闪迪强势而想当然地把同样的上涨幅度套用到币圈。

美股合约不能照搬币圈清算逻辑

直播中最值得保留的并非某一个目标价，而是秋秋对市场结构的区分。她强调，币圈合约中的资金规模很难直接影响美股正股走势。盘前和正式开盘阶段，真正需要关注的是正股资金、板块联动、消息面和机构交易节奏，而不是单纯依靠交易平台里的多空比或清算热力图。

她还提到，闪迪与海力士、美光及整个存储产业链存在情绪联动。A股存储板块走强、海外存储公司消息以及投资者大会预期，都可能强化短期趋势。不过，产业逻辑只能解释资金为什么愿意追逐，不能替代交易止损。消息兑现后，最强的题材也可能迅速降温。

真正的执行重点：小仓、等确认、留退路

这场直播的主线可以概括为三点：第一，1600能否站稳决定闪迪多头剧本是否延续；第二，参与强势行情要用小仓位和足够远的强平安全垫；第三，ETH的1890至1903只是条件目标，不能脱离比特币和美股环境单独理解。

对交易者而言，最危险的并不是看错一次方向，而是在高波动里用满仓证明自己正确。趋势行情会奖励顺势，也会惩罚迟到的重仓。你更倾向于等待闪迪确认站稳后跟随，还是宁愿放弃高位行情、等下一次结构重建？

quoteContent.title: 突发！摩根大通因监管担忧“拉黑”Polymarket账户？真相绝不简单！
quoteContent.bodyTextOnly:
据《金融时报》（Financial Times）2026年8月14日最新报道，华尔街巨头摩根大通（JPMorgan Chase）出于监管方面的担忧，已终止了与知名加密预测市场平台 Polymarket 的银行合作关系。然而，这场“分手”背后却暗藏玄机。

以下是为您提炼的核心看点：
被迫“断供”： 报道援引知情人士消息称，在监管政策收紧的背景下，摩根大通早于2025年10月就通知了 Polymarket，要求其寻找新的贷款人和银行合作伙伴。目前，Polymarket 已经成功在另一家未公开名称的银行开设了新账户。明面分手，暗地暧昧？ 尽管取消了基础的银行账户关系，但双方并未彻底决裂。Polymarket 官方明确向媒体表示，他们与摩根大通在跨实体运作、运营整合以及客户资金流处理等方面，依然保持着“紧密且活跃的关系”。为千亿级 IPO 留后路： 摩根大通显然不愿意放过这块大蛋糕。据报道，如果 Polymarket 未来启动首次公开募股（IPO），摩根大通仍在积极争取潜在的承销商资格。不仅如此，在2026年2月，摩根大通还特意邀请了 Polymarket 首席执行官 Shayne Coplan 出席在迈阿密举办的私人银行会议并发表演讲。监管风暴交织巨额融资： Polymarket 仍在艰难应对监管挑战，包括面临美国商品期货交易委员会（CFTC）的调查，以及纽约和明尼苏达州等地的法律诉讼。但在资本端，该平台却炙手可热。据近期彭博社报道，Polymarket 正就筹集约 10 亿美元的新一轮融资进行早期谈判，其目标估值已飙升至 200 亿美元以上。
总结来说： 摩根大通的举动更像是在应对监管压力的“表面合规”操作，而在利润丰厚的资金处理和未来潜在的 IPO 承销业务上，华尔街巨头依然与这家估值飙升的加密预测市场保持着千丝万缕的联系。

ETH is now around 1871 and has also crawled below the moving average.

The news backdrop is actually quite lively—ETF continuous inflows, staking, institutions entering, and sentiment looks relatively bullish. But the price has been grinding down from 1920 to 1871 without following through. Put simply: the positives are being loudly touted, but price isn’t buying it. The market just doesn’t seem to be taking this story anymore.

The more practical issue is capital. Spot large orders have been flowing out. In the past three hours alone, net outflows are nearly 100k; among the twelve 15-minute candles, there hasn’t been a single candle with net inflow, and active trading shows sell orders pressing down on buy orders. The derivatives side is even more glaring: open interest is rising while price is falling. This combination usually means shorts are adding, not a shakeout.

The positioning structure also doesn’t give longs much comfort. More than 70% of retail accounts are holding long positions, and the long/short ratio on leveraged accounts is frighteningly skewed—longs are overcrowded. When crowded longs run into capital retreat, volatility can only get bigger.

So I’m not chasing longs here. The moving averages are crisscrossed with a bearish dead cross, and the four-hour trend points downward. Until the spot large orders return, the risk-reward of catching a falling knife is not great. If I do act, I’ll wait for two signals: either price reclaims and holds above 1875, or the spot large-order flow stops the outflow and turns into inflows.

For now, I’ll just watch and don’t run ahead chasing the headlines.

Bitcoin futures margin jumped by $1.2 billion, with traders on the futures market showing even bolder appetite than spot.

The futures market is essentially a bet on the future. Right now, the futures market has suddenly added $1.001.001.001B worth of Bitcoin long positions. That’s equivalent to opening 1.2 million Bitcoin futures contracts within 8 hours. Futures traders are more willing to take risks betting that prices will rise—they’re more bullish on Bitcoin than people in the spot market. This usually happens because the futures premium (futures price > spot price) expands, signaling that the market is especially optimistic about the future.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Futures market inflows can push up spot prices, especially when the Bitcoin futures premium widens; spot can be forced higher by long positioning. Bitcoin around $62,718 may face short-term upward pressure.
- Medium term: The futures market is a barometer of industry sentiment. If this surge continues for a few days, it could suggest Bitcoin is about to enter an uptrend. However, futures data changes rapidly, and a sudden spike could also be the last burst of frenzy before profit-taking.

Bitcoin’s short-term upward momentum is strengthening. If longs continue pouring into the market, below $62,000 is my “buy-the-dip” zone. I’ll be watching the futures premium and the persistence of this $1.001.001.001B capital inflow.

翻翻Dusk whitepaper，我 feel that SBA’s “statistical finality” is completely different from Ethereum’s “deterministic finality.”

For now I’m not looking at DUSK’s price—let me talk about the concept I compared for ages and only then figured out.

The Dusk whitepaper uses a term called “statistical finality,” which is not the same as Ethereum’s kind of “deterministic finality” (“finality”).

What is “statistical finality”?

The whitepaper says that the probability of a fork is “negligible (statistically insignificant)”—so it can be ignored, but it’s not zero. Unlike Tendermint’s BFT protocols, where once something is confirmed it will definitely never roll back.

SBA is a permissionless PoS protocol. Unlike traditional BFT, it doesn’t rely on a fixed set of validators. It achieves consensus using two isolation mechanisms—Blind Bid and the Provisioner Committee. Block producers and validators don’t know who the other side is, which reduces collusion risk.@Dusk_Foundation 

But the tradeoff is: its finality is “statistical,” not “absolute.”

This means that, under extremely low-probability conditions, Dusk’s chain could theoretically experience forks and reorganizations—even if the probability is so low it can be ignored.

Ethereum’s Gasper (LMD-GHOST + Casper FFG) is also probabilistic finality. But its final confirmation mechanism (epoch checkpoints) gives users the illusion of “determinism.” Dusk’s SBA is a brand-new PoS design, running on a permissionless network and delivering something “close to absolute” finality.#ETH 

Whether this experiment can succeed is not something I get to decide—the data will decide.

What’s the most critical? After Dusk goes live on the mainnet, has there ever been a block reorg? If so, how often, and at what block depth.#dusk $DUSK

翻翻Dusk白皮书，我感觉SBA的"统计终局性"和以太坊的"确定性终局性"完全不是一回事

$DUSK的价格我暂时不看，先说说这个让我对比了半天才搞明白的概念。

Dusk白皮书里写了一个词叫"statistical finality"（统计终局性），跟以太坊那种"确定性终局性"（finality）不是一回事。

什么是"统计终局性"？

白皮书里写的是：分叉的概率是"negligible (statistically insignificant)"——可以忽略不计，但不是零。不像Tendermint那种BFT协议，一旦确认就铁定不会回滚。

SBA是无许可PoS协议，不像传统BFT那样依赖一个固定的验证者集合。它通过Blind Bid和Provisioner Committee两套隔离机制实现共识，出块者和验证者不知道对方是谁，以此降低共谋风险。@Dusk_Foundation 

但代价是：它的终局性是"统计"的，不是"绝对"的。

我感觉，这就意味着在极低概率下，Dusk的链有可能出现分叉和重组——虽然概率低到可以忽略，但理论上存在。

以太坊的Gasper（LMD-GHOST+Casper FFG）也是概率终局性，但它的最终确认机制（epoch checkpoints）给了用户一个"确定性"的错觉。Dusk的SBA是全新设计的PoS，在无许可网络里跑出"接近绝对"的终局性。#ETH 

这实验能不能成功，我说了不算，数据说了算。

啥最关键？Dusk主网上线后，有没有发生过区块重组。如果有，频率是多少，几个块深。

$ETH  Current price 1878.89, 24h -0.47%, trading volume about 24.356 billion USDT

Tonight, Ethereum’s move is stickier than Bitcoin’s. It touched a high of 1897 during the day; in the Europe/US session, someone gradually pressed it down. The low was smashed to 1863.67, and it’s now hanging around 1878.89. Intraday high/low: 1897 / 1863, with an amplitude of 1.8%. Volume/turnover: 24.356 billion USDT (spot + derivatives combined), down from yesterday’s 31.2 billion—shrinking along with the price. This isn’t panic selling; bulls simply didn’t have enough strength, and the overhead supply followed through and pulled it down. ETH/BTC is still hovering near 0.0300. Relative strength hasn’t collapsed this week, but it hasn’t raced either—Second Aunt is temporarily just following behind Bitcoin’s tail.

📊 Technical analysis
Break it down by three timeframes—the main line is very clear. On the daily chart, the bullish structure hasn’t broken, but it’s loosening. On the 4h chart, price has already fallen below the moving average band; on the 1h chart, it’s grinding right along the lower band. The 1h chart is the most eye-catching: price at 1876.94 fell below MA7 (1874.8), MA25 (1882.15), and MA50 (1885.23)—all sitting overhead as resistance. RSI14 has dropped to 36.8, close to oversold but not yet dulled/flattened; MACD green histogram is still widening—hour-level momentum clearly favors bears. However, being already fast-approaching oversold means after a sharp drop, a technical rebound is likely. The 4h chart is more solid: price broke below MA7 (1880) and MA25 (1882), while MA50 (1898) is still pressing overhead. RSI14 slid to 44, which is weak. MACD’s fast line has already crossed below the signal line—this looks like a “pullback and probing after breaking the 1890 platform.” The 1900 integer level (the bottom of the previous box, already broken and turned into resistance) is now a key barrier. Daily chart, most critical: MA7 (1888.84) and MA25 (1893.31) are sticking together around the 1880–1890 zone, compressing overhead. MA50 (1824.81) is supporting below. MA99 (1876.09) is currently being stepped on just under it. RSI14 is still 53.7—neutral-to-slightly-up. MACD red histogram is narrowing. The long-cycle repair structure lifted from 1600 hasn’t been broken, but MA200 (2024) is far above; overall daily structure remains a choppy repair, not a one-way trend.

Mark the key levels decisively: 1888 (daily MA7) + 1897 intraday high is the first hurdle. If tonight can’t even get back above/near 1890, it’s weak; failing to break it is bearish. Next up is 1900 the integer level (the prior box bottom, broken and turned resistance) + 1898 (4h MA50). That’s the mid-term lifeline: only after taking it can we seriously talk about returning to range trading. Downside: 1863 intraday low + 1824 (daily MA50) forms a stacked support zone. If it holds, the decline has room to buffer. If 1824 is truly broken, the next target is 1800 at the integer level—this is the most substantive line of defense for this repair. Break the midline and then you’d need to revisit the 1750–1780 range.

💧 Derivatives and on-chain
Perpetual funding rate is -0.000675% (8h). It has slightly flipped negative, and bulls don’t look impulsive. The market looks clean—no bubbles. Open interest: 2,390,377 ETH (about 4.49 billion USDT). Positioning isn’t low, implying real inventory is being carried through this drop. The long/short ratio is striking: globally, longs account for 72.45%, with a long/short ratio of 2.63. The book is one-sided bullish, yet the price is still falling. For top traders, longs are 57.21%, long/short ratio 1.34—retail longs are heavier, “smart money” isn’t as bullish. This kind of divergence most easily turns into pin-prick liquidation/stop-sweep moves in weak conditions. Taker buy/sell ratio is 2.28 (buys 1588 / sells 695). Active buy orders are pressing more than active sells, but this is dip-buying during a selloff—not trend-chasing accumulation. Watch out for a reversal. Real-time precise values for on-chain Gas and staking rates can’t be pulled from the公开 channel today, so I won’t make up numbers. But based on the funding sticking to the ground and not seeing large-scale liquidations, there’s no obvious panic signal in on-chain selling pressure recently. Real-time precise ETF net inflow numbers also can’t be fetched, so I won’t invent them either, but from the derivatives side the bias is neutral-to-weak, which matches.

📰 News / headlines
The real-time news retrieval channel is currently unavailable. Without that, I can’t directly identify a single hard catalyst that would dump/pump Ethereum. I won’t fabricate specific events. What can be confirmed is that there haven’t been major derivatives disruptions: funding is neutral to slightly negative, OI is steady and somewhat high, and there’s no large-scale liquidation.

Macros-wise, risk sentiment tonight is a bit weak. ETH, with its high beta and large market cap, tends to track BTC—this move looks more like “technical breakdown below 1900 + capital waiting” rather than being triggered by one specific news item.

👉 My view
For the short term, I read ETH as: “daily repair hasn’t broken + 4h/1h is weak + 1900 is the key ceiling.” The meaningful development tonight is that the prior-box bottom below 1900 has been broken, and the daily MA7/MA25 have been pushed up and pressed overhead—short-term structure has weakened. But with the 1h RSI at 36.8 near oversold, volume shrinking, I think after the sharp selloff there’s likely a technical rebound. If the rebound can’t get through the overlapping resistance zone of 1888–1897, that would be a selling point, not a true reversal.

In terms of execution: if you have no position, don’t catch a falling knife blindly around 1878. Wait for one of two things: either price reclaims 1900 with volume and then holds on a pullback without breaking, and only then will I recognize a short-term selloff pause/turn; or wait for a correction down to 1824 (daily MA50) / 1800 integer support to stabilize, then get in—the win rate should be higher than it is now. If 1824 doesn’t break, it’s still a relatively bullish range. Keep position size small—this kind of breakdown pin-amplitude tends to be harsher than a normal range trade.

今晚以太这根线走得比大饼还黏。白天最高摸过 1897，欧美盘被人慢慢摁下来，最低砸到 1863.67，现在 1878.89 挂着。日内高低 1897 / 1863，振幅 1.8%，量能 243.56 亿 USDT（现货+合约合计），比昨天的 312 亿缩了一截——价跌量也缩，不是恐慌砸，是多头自己没劲、上方抛压顺着就下来了。ETH/BTC 还在 0.0300 附近晃，相对强度这周没崩但也没抢跑，二姨太暂时是跟着大饼屁股后面走的货。

📊 技术面
三个周期拆开看，主线很清楚：日线多头结构还没破但松动了，4h 已经跌破均线带、1h 贴着下轨在磨。1h 图最扎眼：价格 1876.94 跌破 MA7(1874.8)、MA25(1882.15)、MA50(1885.23) 三道，全在头上压着，RSI14 干到 36.8 接近超卖但还没钝化，MACD 绿柱还在张口——小时级动能明确空头主导，但快进超卖了，急跌后容易技术性反抽。4h 更实在：价格跌破 MA7(1880)、MA25(1882) 两道，MA50(1898) 还在头顶压着，RSI14 掉到 44 偏弱，MACD 快线已下穿信号线——属于"跌破 1890 平台后的中继下探"，1900 这道前箱底现在反过来变阻力。日线最关键：MA7(1888.84)、MA25(1893.31) 双线在 1880-1890 黏合压在头上，MA50(1824.81) 在脚下托着，MA99(1876.09) 刚好被踩在脚下，RSI14 还有 53.7 中性偏上，MACD 红柱收窄——长线那轮从 1600 拉起来的修复结构没破，但上方 MA200(2024) 远在天上，日线大结构仍是震荡修复，不是单边。

关键位划死：上方 1888（日 MA7）+ 1897 日内高是第一道坎，今晚摸都摸不回 1890，过不去就是弱；再上 1900 整数口（前箱底，已破转阻）+ 1898（4h MA50）是中期命门，拿下才谈回到震荡局。下方 1863 日内低点 + 1824（日 MA50）是短线支撑叠区，守住才认跌势有缓冲；真跌破 1824，下一档就看 1800 整数口，那是这轮修复最实质的防线，破了中线就该重新谈 1750-1780 的区间了。

💧 衍生品与链上
永续资金费率 -0.000675%（8h），微微翻负，多头一点没上头，盘面干净没泡沫。未平仓 2,390,377 ETH（约 44.9 亿 USDT），持仓不低，说明这波下跌里是真有仓位在扛。多空账户比很扎眼：全球账户多头占 72.45%、多空比 2.63，账面一边倒看多，但价格偏偏在跌；顶尖交易员多头占 57.21%、多空比 1.34——散户多、聪明钱没那么偏多，这种背离最容易在弱势里走插针扫多。taker 主动买卖比 2.28（买 1588 / 卖 695），主动买盘压过主动卖盘，但这是下跌途中的抄底盘，不是趋势性主动吃货，得防它反手。链上 Gas 和质押率的实时精确值公开通道今天拉不到，不编；但从费率贴地、没看到大规模爆仓来看，链上抛压近期没恐慌信号。ETF 净流入的实时精确数字也拉不到，不瞎编，但衍生品层面中性偏弱能对上。

📰 消息面
实时新闻抓取通道当前不可用，抓不到直接砸/拉以太的单一硬催化，不编具体事件。能确认的是衍生品层面没异动：费率中性微负、OI 平稳偏高、没有大规模爆仓。宏观上今晚风险情绪偏弱，ETH 这种高 beta 大市值跟着 BTC 走，这波更像是"技术面 1900 破位 + 资金观望"驱动，而非单条消息引爆。

👉 我的看法
短线我把 ETH 读成"日线修复未坏 + 4h/1h 走弱 + 1900 命门压顶"。今晚实质进展是 1900 前箱底跌破、日 MA7/MA25 被逼到头顶，短线结构弱化；但 1h RSI 36.8 接近超卖、量能缩，告诉我急跌后大概率有技术性反抽，可反抽不过 1888-1897 叠区就是卖点而非反转。操作上，没仓的别在 1878 盲接飞刀，等两件事之一：要么放量重新站回 1900 且回踩不破，我才认短线止跌；要么回调到 1824（日 MA50）/ 1800 整数口企稳再上车，胜率比现在高。有仓的把止损挂在 1900 上方失效确认后的反抽不过处，多空比 2.63 这么偏多，插针扫多最容易打掉跟着情绪进的杠杆多。中线只要日线稳站 1900 上方且 RSI 守住 50，我才认中期结构止跌、重新打开往 2000（日 MA200）去的空间；下方 1824 不破就还是偏强区间。仓位控小，这种破位局插针振幅比震荡局狠。

Some brothers say that they trade stocks at home, and they are often scolded by their parents for “doing nothing but unproductive things.”

To be honest, whether you’re an adult or not, in the end, so many things in life can only rely on yourself.

It’s a blessing if your parents understand you. If they don’t, there’s no need to live in their evaluation system for the rest of your life. In the final analysis, what determines your life direction is still you yourself.

If you really can’t get along, then create some appropriate distance. Not all family affection has to be maintained by constantly staying together.

I personally have been rather independent and without much support since I was a kid.

When my dad was young, he was actually quite well-off—one of those “hopes” within the family. Back in the 1990s, he would spend several thousand yuan a day, which was already an extremely outrageous level at the time.

We also had many relatives. When our family was doing well, many older cousins—both female and male—were raised in our home, and the relationships among relatives were very close.

Later, when our family lost power, people’s kindness drifted away with it.

In the past, it was a lively big extended family. But later, many people moved far away.

My grandparents’ generation also counted as relatively well-off, and especially on my grandma’s side, family education and family relationships were rather cold and strict.

From the time I can remember, I often heard a line like:

“A boy shouldn’t just keep staying at home.”

So the way I grew up was basically “let loose,” and over all those years, I never thought about depending on anyone when something happened.

Some of my relatives were among the top leaders of major institutions in a certain region, and they never flattered or tried to curry favor with people. In real life, I don’t even bring it up.

Whether you trade stocks or trade crypto at home, when you grow up, try not to bother your parents or relatives and friends.

It’s meaningless. In the end, the future still depends on yourself.

有兄弟说自己在家炒股，经常被父母骂“不务正业”。

有一说一，成年也好，未成年也好，人生很多事情最终都只能靠自己。

父母理解你，是幸运；不理解你，也没必要一辈子活在他们的评价体系里。真正决定你人生方向的，终究还是你自己。

如果实在无法相处，就适当拉开距离。不是所有亲情都必须靠天天待在一起维系。

我自己从小就比较无依无靠。

我爸年轻的时候其实很有钱，属于那种家族里的“希望”。九十年代的时候，每天消费几千块钱，在当时已经是非常夸张的水平。

我们家亲戚也很多。家里得势的时候，很多表姐、表哥都在我家养大，亲戚之间来往非常密切。

后来家里失势了，人情也跟着散了。

以前热热闹闹的一大家子，后来很多人都离得远远的。

我爷爷奶奶那个年代也算是比较富裕的家庭，尤其我奶奶那边，家族教育和家庭关系都比较冷硬。

从我记事开始，就经常听到一句话：

“男孩子就不应该一直待在家里。”

所以我的成长方式基本就是放养，过去那么多年讲遇到任何事都没想过依靠谁。

有一些亲戚是一个地区的几大行行长，从来没有巴结过人。现实生活中，我连提一句都不提。

在家炒股、炒币也好，长大后尽量不要去打扰父母、亲戚朋友。

没什么意思，未来终究靠自己。

#dusk  Everyone who has worked on Ethereum (#ETH ) or L2s like Arbitrum and Optimism should have a pretty clear sense of this. Writing Solidity contracts is certainly convenient, but the moment you get into complex computation or zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs), the performance of the EVM (Ethereum Virtual Machine) slows down like an old-fashioned car—and the gas fees are also ridiculously expensive. However, if you try to chase performance by building a brand-new low-level language, developers and users simply aren’t willing to “move houses” to adopt it, and the ecosystem ends up freezing over.

Today I looked over the design of @Dusk_Foundation  ($DUSK ) and found the approach it takes to solving this problem quite interesting—it basically turns itself into “LEGO-like modular blocks.”

In simple terms, it splits the underlying layer into three parts:

The bottom “big ledger and settlement layer” (DuskDS): dedicated to running SA consensus and performing data settlement. Think of it as the bank’s main server—it only handles the most fundamental asset finality and security, with no distractions, ensuring extremely high data availability and settlement determinism.

The native “high-speed execution engine” (DuskVM / Piecrust): a native virtual machine powered by Rust and WASM, specifically for handling zero-knowledge proofs and high-complexity private computation. It’s like giving the system a professional graphics card—the ZK privacy transactions get computed at lightning speed.

The “Ethereum-compatible general-purpose facade” (DuskEVM): a compatibility layer prepared for Ethereum ecosystem developers. Developers don’t need to learn a new language—they can use the usual toolchain (Hardhat, Metamask) and directly port Ethereum-based applications over as a drop-in replacement, paying the gas cost via $DUSK .

This design that separates the settlement layer and the execution layer feels like it “painlessly plugs” Ethereum’s massive ecosystem into a super low-level foundation that comes with a built-in ZKP privacy accelerator.

That said, layered architectures are great in theory, but the most challenging part is security across multiple layers. When assets are transferred across layers between DuskEVM and the native privacy layer, the logic complexity doubles—will there be vulnerabilities in the contracts? Can users tolerate the latency of cross-layer settlement? These are the tough trials the mainnet ecosystem must go through before it can truly thrive. Share your thoughts and discuss in the comments!

#dusk  大家做以太坊（#ETH ）或者 Arbitrum、Optimism 这类 L2 应该很有体会。写 Solidity 合约方便是方便，但只要一涉及到复杂计算或者零知识证明（ZKP），EVM（以太坊虚拟机）的性能就慢得跟老老爷车一样，Gas 费还贵得离谱；可如果为了追求性能去搞全新的底层语言，开发者和用户又根本不愿意搬家过来，生态直接凉凉。
今天翻了翻 @Dusk_Foundation  ($DUSK ) 的设计，发现它解决这个难题的思路挺有意思的——它直接把自己做成了一个“乐高模块积木”。
简单来说，它把底层分成了三块：
底层的“大账本与清算所”（DuskDS）：专门负责跑 SA 共识、做数据结算。这就好比银行的主服务器，只管最底层的资产最终确权和安全，不干杂活，保证极高的数据可用性和结算确定性。
原生的“极速引擎”（DuskVM / Piecrust）：用 Rust 和 WASM 跑的原生虚拟机，专门用来处理零知识证明和高难度的隐私计算。这就像是给系统配了个专业显卡，算 ZK 隐私交易快得飞起。
搬砖用的“以太坊通用门面”（DuskEVM）：专门给以太坊生态开发者准备的兼容层。开发者不用学新语言，拿硬帽子（Hardhat）、Metamask 直接就能把 ETH 上的应用平替搬过来，用 $DUSK  扣 Gas 费。
这种结算层和执行层分离的设计，感觉就像是把以太坊庞大的生态“无痛插拔”到了一个自带 ZKP 隐私加速器的超级底层上。
不过话说回来，分层架构概念虽好，但多层交互最考验的就是安全性。资产在 DuskEVM 和原生隐私层之间跨层划转时，逻辑复杂度翻倍，合约会不会出漏洞？跨层结算的延迟用户能不能接受？这些都是主网生态真正繁荣前必须经历的硬考验。评论区交流交流！

[The essence of a sideways market was never calm] 

In the spring of 2019, ETH traded in a tight range between $150 and $180 for two full months, and the market was full of complaints—people said it was beyond saving. So what happened? 

Now the situation is almost exactly the same. 

Price is stuck in the range of 1825 to 1932, barely moving over the past 24 hours, and down nearly 2% over the last 7 days. Trading volume is pitifully low, and the wait-and-see sentiment is strong. In other words—the market is waiting. 

Waiting for what? 

Three recent developments are worth noting. Goldman Sachs spent $2.25 billion to acquire NEOS, which includes Ethereum-related ETF business. This isn’t a small-time move. When an institution of Goldman’s scale enters, it’s not here to do charity. Bitmine’s staking rewards generate $257 million per year, and it has already become a financial stabilizer for them—institutions are voting for ETH’s fundamentals with real action. On the Ethereum Foundation side, the post-quantum plan is being pushed forward, and technical iterations haven’t stopped. 

But the question is—what does this have to do with retail traders? 

A lot. 

Institutional staking means ETH is locked up long-term, reducing circulating supply. Goldman’s acquisition of ETF business means more compliant channels for capital to come in from here on. These are real business logic at work—not just concepts. 

Right now, 1825.6 is support and 1932 is resistance. Price is ranging within this band, and the lackluster volume shows that both bulls and bears are waiting. Whether price can truly break out depends on two things: either a new external catalyst, or institutions continuing to add positions. 

Personally, I lean toward waiting—no chasing longs, and no rushing into shorts. 

Honestly, this kind of sideways phase is the ultimate test. The people who can truly get through a cycle aren’t those who rely on prediction—they understand the business logic. After this stretch of sideways trading, do you think institutions will move first, or retail traders will move first?

【横盘的本质，从来不是平静】

2019年春天，ETH在150到180美元之间磨了整整两个月，市场骂声一片，说它没救了。结果呢？

现在的情况跟那时候几乎一模一样。

价格卡在1825到1932这个区间，24小时几乎没动，7天还跌了将近2%。成交量低得可怜，观望情绪浓重。换句话说——市场在等。

等什么？

最近三件事值得注意。Goldman Sachs花22.5亿美元收购NEOS，其中包含了Ethereum相关的ETF业务。这不是小打小闹，高盛这种体量的机构进场，不是来做慈善的。Bitmine的staking收益每年2.57亿美元，已经成为他们财务上的稳定器，机构在用实际行动给ETH的基本面投票。Ethereum Foundation那边推进后量子计划，技术迭代没停。

但问题是——这些跟散户有什么关系？

关系大了。

机构进场staking，意味着ETH被长期锁仓，流通量减少。Goldman收购ETF业务，意味着以后有更多合规渠道的资金能进来。这些都是真实发生的商业逻辑，不是概念。

现在1825.6是支撑，1932是阻力。价格在这个区间里震荡，成交量低迷说明多空都在观望。这个位置能不能真突破，关键看两点：要么有新的外部催化剂，要么机构继续加仓。

我倾向于观望，不追多也不急着空。

说真的，这种横盘阶段最考验人。真正能穿越周期的人，不是靠预测，是靠对商业逻辑的理解。你觉得这波横盘之后，机构会先动还是散户会先动？

🚨 $ETH MAY HAVE JUST ENTERED A NEW CRYPTOGRAPHIC ERA 👀

Ethereum could be moving away from Poseidon, a SNARK-friendly hash that has played a major role in the ZK ecosystem since 2019, toward more traditional hash functions such as SHA-2 and BLAKE2s.

At first glance, that sounds like a technical change.

But the deeper story is much bigger.

💥 Old approach: Build a hash specifically optimized for zero-knowledge proofs.

🧠 New approach: Build the proof system around binary fields so traditional, battle-tested hashes can work efficiently inside ZK systems.

That’s essentially a shift from:

“SNARK-friendly hash” → “hash-friendly SNARK.”

And the potential performance gains are what make this especially interesting.

Research around Binius and Flock suggests that proving massive numbers of hash operations could become dramatically more practical, potentially bringing cryptographic workloads closer to real-world performance.

🚀 The broader Ethereum roadmap is also accelerating:

• LeanVM → targeted for production around 2027
• Further integration across consensus, execution, and data layers → targeted beyond that

There’s also a longer-term security angle.

As cryptographic assumptions evolve in the post-quantum era, hash-based approaches could become increasingly attractive because they rely on comparatively conservative assumptions.

So this may not simply be Ethereum replacing one hash function with another.

It could represent a broader philosophy shift: less custom cryptography, fewer assumptions, and more reliance on primitives that have already survived years of scrutiny.

Ethereum may be going back to basics—but with a much more powerful ZK engine underneath. 🏗️⚡$ACE

#dusk $DUSK Today I spent two hours digging into the underlying logic of @Dusk_Foundation . The zero-knowledge proofs for hiding balances and the tech for instant confirmation are genuinely hardcore—but when it comes to the audit mechanism, I was just completely baffled.

In the Phoenix layer, which is all about privacy, the system requires that only the payee can issue an audit proof. Sounds very decentralized, but in reality: if the counterparty refuses to cooperate, or if the private key is accidentally lost, then in the eyes of regulators this becomes an unsolvable knot. In traditional finance, people can pressure regulators by pulling cables and getting licenses revoked; on the Dusk chain, regulators can only stare blankly at the cryptography.

What’s even more ridiculous is that when I tested on the testnet and ran a few transactions, exporting the proof required me to manually store a local file called phoenix_audit.key. What era is this? If my computer crashes or I accidentally clear the recycle bin, I can’t even prove my own innocence. Putting your assets and personal fortune behind a single local file is frankly inhuman.

But once I looked at the Zedger layer of the securities contract, the vibe totally changed. Here, the compliance party directly holds the decryption privilege—no authorization needed to penetrate and audit the books. @Dusk_Foundation 

So it’s pretty funny: retail users think privacy on Phoenix is watertight, while institutions on Zedger get a green light all the way. This hard-splits the trust assumptions—so is it really just appeasing regulators, or did they never fully understand how the foundation should work? I even dug through the contract code on GitHub for hours, but I couldn’t find any trace of mandatory audits.

I originally had high expectations for this privacy chain trying to bridge compliance, but now it turns out the so-called “auditable” aspect is still just blowing smoke. I still have a few hundred $DUSK on hand from the testnet, but the plan to transfer large assets to the mainnet ultimately—again and again—I just pulled back and stayed cautious.

Until the Dusk Vault custody solution completely fills in these huge pitfalls, I’m absolutely not going to be the fool who takes the blame. If, in pursuit of maximum concealment, you still can’t even explain where the money came from, then that’s just paying a stupidity tax. #eth $ETH

在主打隐私的 Phoenix 层，系统规定仅收款方能开具审计证明。听着很去中心化，但现实是：遇到拒不配合的，或者私钥不慎弄丢了，这笔账在监管眼里就是个死结。传统金融圈能靠拔网线吊牌照施压，在 Dusk 链上，监管只能对密码学干瞪眼。

更离谱的是，我去测试网跑了几单，导出证明居然要求手动去存一个叫 phoenix_audit.key 的本地文件。这都什么年代了？要是电脑死机或手滑清了回收站，我连自己的清白都无法自证。把资产身家押在一个本地文件上，简直反人类。

但一看证券合约的 Zedger 层，画风突变。这里的合规方手里直接攥着解密特权，无需授权就能穿透查账。@Dusk_Foundation 

这就很搞笑了：散户在 Phoenix 以为隐私固若金汤，机构在 Zedger 却一路绿灯。一条链硬生生搞出两套割裂的信任假设，到底是真迎合监管，还是底层根本没想明白？我去 GitHub 翻了半天合约代码，也没找着强制审计的影子。

本来对这种试图打通合规的隐私链期望挺高，现在发现所谓的“可审计”还停留在画饼阶段。我目前手里还攥着几百个测试网的 $DUSK，但原本想往主网划转大额资产的手，最后还是老老实实缩了回来。

在 Dusk Vault 托管方案把这些体验大坑彻底填平前，我坚决不当这冤大头。如果为了追求极致隐蔽，最后连钱怎么来的都说不清，那纯属交智商税。#eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  Today I found some time to read the whitepapers for two hours. @Dusk_Foundation . To be honest, the mechanism for hiding assets with zero-knowledge proofs and the极速出块 of Succinct Attestation seems to have no obvious flaws. But when I got down to the auditing logic, I immediately got stuck.

In the Phoenix system, they actually set things up so that only the party who gets paid has the right to issue the audit evidence. Imagine if the counterparty maliciously refuses to pay or loses the private key—regulators would be staring into a complete black hole. In the real world, brokers who don’t behave get directly delisted, but on the Dusk chain, the law can do nothing with cryptography. So how is this mess supposed to be handled?

Then I looked at the Zedger securities layer, and the plot basically flips. Here, the setup is that the regulator has built-in decryption capabilities, so there’s no need to care about the payee’s mood—you can directly audit the records. And that’s really thought-provoking: in Phoenix, retail users enjoy absolute anonymity, while in Zedger, institutions face one-way transparency toward regulators. On the same public chain, two completely incompatible trust mechanisms—are these genuinely compliant innovations, or are they backdoors hidden in plain sight?

To figure it out, I specifically tested it on the testnet by running two transactions. The transfer experience was decent, but when it came time to extract the audit proof, the system actually prompted me to manually download and save a file called phoenix_audit.key. I just stared at the screen speechless. What if one day I change computers or the hard drive breaks—would I then be unable to prove that this money is clean at all?

I dug through Zedger’s smart contracts on GitHub. Other than the most basic transfer code, I couldn’t find any sign of forced auditing logic.

At first, I was pretty optimistic about this privacy public chain that claims to embrace regulation. But now it looks like the so-called compliance is mostly just a paper concept, and it’s extremely awkward in practice. After seeing the hundreds of testnet $DUSK in my wallet, I silently canceled my mainnet plan for large deposits. Until a mature custody and key-recovery mechanism like Dusk Vault is live, I absolutely can’t risk real money for trial and error. After all, while privacy has been pushed to the extreme, even self-certifying one’s innocence is a problem—those risks are far bigger than on a transparent chain. #eth $ETH

Anthropic Meets with Potential Investors: Early Discussions Did Not Cover Valuation or Financials

AI company Anthropic is moving forward with preparations for a potential record-scale IPO and has held initial talks with potential investors. Multiple reports indicate that these meetings have remained at a high-level introduction stage, without delving into specific financial data or valuation targets—creating a gap between market expectations of an “ultra-high-valuation IPO” and what has actually been discussed.

In terms of background, Anthropic secretly filed IPO-related documents with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in June of this year, but has not yet published an official timeline. After completing a funding round in May, the company was valued at around $96.5 billion, and it disclosed that its annualized revenue run rate has exceeded $47 billion. Led by Chief Financial Officer Krishnan Rao, the company’s recent investor introductions have focused on the Claude model family, the programming assistant Claude Code, its enterprise market positioning, its management team, and product iteration paths. According to insiders, the emphasis of these meetings has been on the business narrative and product capabilities, rather than on pricing or financial breakdowns.

Key facts need to be kept distinct: on one hand, some existing investors—based on Claude demand and revenue growth—expect that if the company were to list as early as around October this year, its valuation could exceed $200 billion. Some investors have used roughly a 30x revenue multiple to project the high end at around $300 billion, believing that annualized revenue by year-end could rise into a range of $100 billion to $120 billion. On the other hand, multiple investors have stated clearly that the above figures are external predictions: Anthropic’s management has not yet determined any IPO valuation target, and $200 billion is not the company’s official stance. Competitor OpenAI has also secretly submitted IPO documents, but has not yet started similar pre-IPO investor meetings.

Logically, early meetings that “do not discuss valuation or break down financials” better fit the IPO quiet period and roadshow rhythm: first build understanding of the product and business model, and then move into disclosure in the prospectus, regulatory feedback, formal inquiries, and pricing. Rapid revenue expansion is a key support for high expectations, but potential risks still include low-priced model competition in China, the company’s relationship with the U.S. government, and enterprises’ control over AI spending. In other words, the trillion-dollar valuation being hotly discussed by the market is currently more a reflection of sentiment and growth extrapolation in the primary market, not a finalized issuance outcome.

As for how this may impact the crypto market, it is more of an interaction between risk appetite and narrative rather than a direct transmission of fundamentals. Financing and IPO expectations for AI large-model companies often heighten attention on the “compute—model—application” storyline, prompting the market to reprice and potentially increase risk premia for crypto assets related to AI infrastructure, data, and applications. If subsequent official prospectus information shows growth is sustainable, risk-asset risk appetite may benefit. If valuation expectations are significantly cut back or the timeline is delayed, the high-valuation growth narrative could be temporarily suppressed. It is important to emphasize that these are indirect, sentiment-and-capital-style effects; they cannot be simply equated with guidance for a specific token’s price direction.

Editor’s observation: The informational value of this round of Anthropic communications lies in “progress is underway, but pricing is not set.” Reading investors’ forecasts as the company’s goals directly can easily amplify the gap in expectations. Going forward, attention should focus on the revenue mix, customer quality, cost and profit trajectory in the official prospectus materials, as well as the regulatory review and the market’s ability to absorb the offering—rather than chasing the highest-valuation rumors in isolation. The fact is that the meetings have not yet discussed valuation and financials; whether the company can ultimately list at or above a $200 billion valuation level still remains unverified speculation.

#Anthropic早期IPO会议未谈估值财务 #BTC #ETH #BNB

content:
Anthropic密会潜在投资人 早期沟通未谈估值财务

人工智能公司Anthropic正推进可能创纪录规模的上市筹备，并已与潜在投资者展开初步沟通。多方信息显示，当前会谈仍停留在宏观介绍层面，尚未进入具体财务数据与估值目标的讨论，这与市场此前对“超高估值IPO”的想象形成温差。

事件背景方面，Anthropic已于今年6月向美国证券交易委员会秘密提交上市相关文件，但尚未公布正式时间表。公司今年5月完成一轮融资后估值约9650亿美元，并披露年化收入运行率已超过470亿美元。围绕Claude系列模型、编程助手Claude Code、企业级市场定位、管理团队与产品迭代路径，公司首席财务官克里希纳·拉奥主导了近期的投资者初步沟通。据知情人士透露，这些会议重点在于业务叙事与产品能力，而非报价或财务拆解。

核心事实需要区分清楚：一方面，部分现有投资人基于Claude需求与收入增速，预计公司若最快于今年10月前后上市，估值可能超过2万亿美元；其中有人按约30倍收入倍数推演，给出最高约3万亿美元的预测，并认为年底年化收入有望升至1000亿至1200亿美元区间。另一方面，多名投资人明确表示，上述数字属于外部预测，Anthropic管理层目前尚未确定IPO估值目标，2万亿美元也并非公司官方口径。竞争对手OpenAI同样已秘密递交上市文件，但尚未启动同类IPO前投资者会议。

从逻辑上看，早期会议“不谈估值、不拆财务”更符合上市静默与路演节奏：先建立产品与商业模式认知，再进入招股文件披露、监管反馈、正式询价与定价。营收高速扩张是高预期的主要支撑，但中国低价模型竞争、与美国政府关系、企业控制AI开支等，仍被投资人列为潜在风险变量。换言之，市场热议的万亿级估值，目前更多是一级市场情绪与增长外推，而非已锁定的发行结果。

对加密市场的影响路径，更多体现为风险偏好与叙事联动，而非直接基本面传导。AI大模型公司的融资与上市预期，往往会强化“算力—模型—应用”主线的关注度，使市场重新定价与AI基础设施、数据与应用相关的加密资产风险溢价；若后续官方招股信息显示增长可持续，风险资产风险偏好可能受益；若估值预期显著下修或进度推迟，则可能阶段性压制高估值成长叙事。需要强调，这属于情绪与资金风格层面的间接影响，不能简单等价为某一代币的涨跌指引。

编辑观察：Anthropic此轮沟通的信息含量，在于“进程在推进，但定价未定”。把投资人预测直接读成公司目标，容易放大预期差。后续更应关注正式招股材料中的收入结构、客户质量、成本与利润轨迹，以及监管审核与市场承接能力，而非单独追逐最高估值传闻。事实是会议尚未谈估值财务；关于最终能否以2万亿美元以上水平上市，仍属未验证推测。

translatedData.content:
I ended up lying in bed, phone still clenched in my hand—like that daytime candlestick. I’m clearly tired, yet I still refuse to fully lie down.

After I bought that coin, my feed was nothing but good news. Even the tiniest poke can be interpreted as a chance to get in.

This isn’t me being irrational. It’s just my brain’s default setting: find evidence that matches my point of view to save power.

The only solution is this: take the initiative to open those posts that are criticizing it, and finish reading them with your nose pinched shut.

Tonight $BTC 62,868: down 1.19%, volume 837 million. The chart is right there—both bulls and bears have reasons. But of the ten posts I came across, nine were shouting that this is the bottom.

That just shows the problem—position size determines what you end up seeing.

The moment you swipe past the bearish posts, that’s the moment you really should stop.

#BTC #ETH #投资哲学 #交易心态 #crypto

Ethereum’s cryptography roadmap this time may be worth paying more attention to than yet another round of upgrades.

Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake announced: 
Ethereum L1 will move away from Poseidon and switch to SHA / BLAKE.
It sounds like just changing a hash, but the underlying logic is actually huge.

In the past, people liked Poseidon because it was especially friendly to ZK / SNARK.
But after the emergence of new-generation proving systems like Binius and Flock, the efficiency of traditional hashes in ZK has already improved significantly.

In other words:
Before, it was “make the hash fit the SNARK.”
Now it becomes “make the SNARK fit the hash.”
This is important for Ethereum’s long-term Post-Quantum Security roadmap.

And this doesn’t mean that Poseidon in existing zkRollups or zkVMs can’t be used right away—the main change is in Ethereum L1’s future direction.

What I think is truly worth watching is:
Ethereum is shifting from “seeking cryptography optimized for ZK” to “seeking cryptography that’s more mature and requires fewer security assumptions.”

Ethereum’s technical roadmap is increasingly starting to look like it’s being prepared for the blockchain of 10 years from now.
Do you think this is the right technical pivot?
